year_meanings.1999: historical reference before large iceberg-era disruption
year_meanings.2001: during iceberg-era change, not same exact intervention onset at all six sites
year_meanings.2024: latest available single breeding-pair aerial census reference

metric: Author published count of breeding pairs in same six named site units; NOT adult survival, fledging success or tracked dispersal.
descriptive_analyses: sum exactly six paired site counts for each of 1999, 2001, 2024; only if all six recorded in each year
individual site changes 1999→2001 and 1999→2024, with clear 2001 shock-severity difference
2024 counterfactual count under fixed 1999 spatial shares and observed total; compare actual to expectation as pure proportional-growth benchmark
1999 size-similar Royds versus Cape Bird Middle difference with initial-shock-severity warning
share of total 1999→2024 net gain contributed by individual named sites
prior_art_vetoes: Regional and Ross Island colony abundance changes already studied (Ainley 2024; Dugger 2026; earlier Ross isotope/census literature).
A descriptive contrast within one Ross Island is not independent island-biogeographic replication.
Proportional-growth benchmark does not identify migration/social settlement effect.
Published 2026 NZ aerial counts may share observational provenance with earlier datasets; separate archive does not prove independent counts.
falsification_conditions: If any of the six names/year source cell missing or nonnumeric, report HOLD_NO_EXACT_PAIRED_SITE_CENSUS; do not fabricate zeros.
If 2024 source contains Royds 0, do not infer biological absence without the survey method, quality and site definition.
Do not interpret changes in breeding pair counts as natal dispersal, adult movement or phenological effects.
Do not claim missed Cape Barne represents an extinct patch.
No model fitted, no p values, no causal inference, no amendments to scientific manuscript PR189.
